newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's IPCA-E inflation index up 2.45 pct in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's IPCA-E inflation index up 2.45 pct in Q1.

text.p: Brazilian inflation as measured by the Special Wider National Consumers Price Index (IPCA-E) was 2.45 percent in the first quarter of 1997, the National Statistics Institute (IBGE) said in a statement on Monday.
The IPCA-E is a quarterly index based on the spending of families with an income of up to 40 minimum salaries. It is used to calculate the Ufir index, which adjusts income tax.
Inflation as measured by the index was 9.92 percent for the whole of 1996 and 2.19 percent in the third quarter of 1996.
The first-quarter reading reflected inflation of 1.13 percent in January, 0.71 percent in February and 0.59 percent in March, the IBGE said.
In the 12 months to the end of March, inflation as measured by the index was 8.82 percent, the IBGE said.
The transport and communications sector registered the highest inflation at 4.45 percent, while the clothing sector showed the greatest reduction with prices falling by 0.33 percent, the IBGE said.
Of the 11 geographical areas surveyed, Belo Horizonte had the highest inflation at 3.22 percent and Recife had the lowest at 1.71 percent.
Rio de Janeiro and Sao Paulo were the only other areas where inflation exceeded the national average, the IBGE said.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
